name: Petra Nnaji-Szymański
description: Petra Nnaji-Szymański emerged from the Shelf's flat-screen underground in the late 2180s, insisting that neural-feed was a tool of cognitive colonization and refusing every corporate offer she received. Her films — shot on salvaged optical rigs and distributed on physical media — are dense, slow, and structurally demanding, built around unaugmented human faces and ambient industrial sound. She has never filed for a Vantablack distribution license and has no intention of doing so.
cultural_impact: She is the central figure of the Flat-Screen Resistance aesthetic — a movement that treats the refusal of neural-feed as a political act, not a technical limitation.
story_hooks: Nnaji-Szymański is reportedly working on a film using footage obtained from inside a corponation facility — footage that could destroy careers and provoke legal retaliation.
A Vantablack talent scout has been tasked with making her an offer she cannot refuse; the player is that scout, or is hired to intercept them.
Her archive of physical media is stored in a Shelf location that is about to be demolished in a corponation infrastructure expansion.
